sections.label: The opening
sections.para: Feasible on open source: PDF.js draws pages in layers and reads attachments, metadata, links and a fingerprint; our layer goes on top, found through clues the PDF carries; the hard parts are the interface, anchors and signing.

sections.label: In short
sections.para: PDF is static; a viewer with an augmented layer; PDF.js exists; clues not contents; precedents; the hard part is not the PDF.

sections.label: Why augment a PDF
sections.para: PDF describes a printed page and has nothing behind it, but it is how documents travel; a viewer could show the layers of the augmented book behind any PDF.

sections.label: A viewer that already exists
sections.para: PDF.js is Apache-licensed, released on 3 October and committed on 30 October, draws pages as canvas, text and annotation layers, and reads what we need; alternatives have licence or maintenance questions.

sections.label: The PDF only needs clues
sections.para: An embedded JSON file, XMP metadata, a link, the file's id looked up on our server, and a QR code that survives printing, tried in order.

sections.label: It has been done, in parts
sections.line: It has been done, in parts
sections.para: Hypothesis anchors notes to PDFs by fingerprint and quote; the W3C model defines anchors; e-invoices carry XML in a PDF; C2PA embeds signed provenance.

sections.label: What not to do: JavaScript inside the PDF
sections.para: PDF JavaScript is heavily attacked and often disabled, so the layer never depends on it; the viewer does the work.

sections.label: How hard is it?
sections.para: PDF.js's viewer plus one layer, discovery through the clues, anchors by quote and page, clues written at build time, and a signed layer: weeks for a prototype.

sections.label: The risks
sections.para: Stripped clues, drifting anchors, faked layers, addresses found in documents, and licences outside PDF.js.

sections.label: What I want to try
sections.para: The RC1 PDF with a signed layer, its id in metadata and QR codes, in a PDF.js viewer and then in the iPad app, still opening normally everywhere else.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.para: A brief; code read, not run; some facts from search only; the weeks an estimate; my interest.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: My message of 31 October, the repositories cloned and read, and search results marked as such.
